data.narrative:
Aigen, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Kenny Lee and Richard Wurden, has raised approximately $23.7M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private peers and one public comparable, concentrated in the robotics and manufacturing sector at similar stage.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implies a valuation of $45M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B)—yields a median valuation of $1.8B, with a range spanning $1.6B to $2.0B.

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range of $38M to $2.0B, with a median of $898M. This disparity reflects a material tension: stage-progression mechanically extends recent capital history, while peer-median anchors to later-stage robotics valuations that may incorporate significantly higher risk-adjusted growth expectations. The appropriate valuation likely clusters toward the lower end of peer range absent evidence of outsized revenue traction or proprietary defensibility beyond peer set. Key uncertainties include revenue visibility, capital efficiency relative to peers, and whether peer valuations reflect sustainable multiples or sector-wide pricing inflection.
